official.deadline_note: No central deadline exists: the guidelines state the deadline for submission of application documents varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission. Recruitment for April/September-October 2027 arrival runs April-May 2026 and first screening May-July 2026, so the mission's own deadline governs.
official.application_cycle: 2027 arrival (April or October term); recruitment April-May 2026, first screening early May to late July 2026, second screening and placement from November 2026, results January to early March 2027
official.status_note: The 2027 cycle's application window (April-May 2026) has passed. MEXT's process chart places first screening between early May and late July 2026, provisional acceptance requests after 1 September 2026, second screening and university placement from November 2026, and notification of results between January and early March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waivered." The entrance examination fee is borne by the grantee if they cannot proceed to a master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of 143,000 yen (preparatory education and non-regular students), 144,000 yen (regular students in master's or professional degree courses) or 145,000 yen (regular students in doctoral courses)
Supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month for study or research in specially designated regions
Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the accepting university waivered
Economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on graduation and return by the end of the scholarship period, back to the home country
Up to six months of Japanese-language preparatory education before placement at the university where the accepting university requires it
eligibility: Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; applicants holding Japanese nationality are not eligible, and dual nationals must relinquish Japanese nationality by the date of arrival in Japan
Born on or after 2 April 1992, with exceptions only where MEXT accepts that the applicant could not apply in time due to their country's circumstances

16 years of school education outside Japan, or an equivalent qualification, for a master's or doctoral (first phase) course; 18 years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary sciences and certain pharmaceutical fields
Willingness to learn Japanese, interest in Japan, and the ability to conduct research and adapt to living in Japan
Health certificate in the prescribed format signed by a physician attesting no physical or mental condition hindering study in Japan
Not a previous grantee of a Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship programme and not applying to another MEXT programme at the same time
requirements: Submit the complete document set to the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality by its designated deadline; submitted documents are not returned
Documents must be written in Japanese or English, or accompanied by a Japanese or English translation
Use the 2027 forms for the Application Form, Placement Preference Application Form, Field of Study and Research Plan and Medical Certificate

After passing first screening, contact up to two universities at a time for a letter of provisional acceptance, using the MEXT-specified format and through the division of international student affairs
Choose the arrival period (April or October term) in the Application Form - in principle it cannot be changed after submission
documents: Application Form (2027 form) with a 4.5 x 3.5 cm photograph taken within six months of submission
Field of Study and Research Plan (2027 form)

Academic transcripts for all academic years of university attended, showing the grade scale, plus a certificate of graduation or degree certificate (certificate of prospective graduation if not yet graduated)
Recommendation letter from the president, dean or academic advisor at the current or last university attended, and a Medical Certificate on the 2027 form

Where applicable: abstracts of theses, a certificate of Japanese or English language proficiency issued within the last two years in three copies, an employer recommendation, and photographs or recorded media of works of art for fine arts and music applicants
selection_criteria: Document screening: academic achievement at the last university attended at or above a certain level, with a detailed and concrete research plan
Written examinations in Japanese and English, both taken by all applicants; the English examination may be exempted for countries where English is the official language
Interview showing a clear sense of purpose about studying in Japan, knowledge of Japanese universities, and sufficient Japanese or English to communicate with an academic advisor
Second screening by MEXT, with placement at one of the three preferred universities that grants provisional acceptance; applications may be rejected on weapons-proliferation concerns
coverage: Monthly scholarship: 143,000 yen (preparatory education and non-regular students), 144,000 yen (master's and professional degree courses), 145,000 yen (doctoral courses), plus a 2,000 or 3,000 yen regional allowance
Tuition, matriculation and entrance examination fees at the university waivered
Economy-class airfare from the international airport nearest the grantee's residence to Japan, and return airfare on graduation if the grantee returns by the end of the scholarship period
Not covered: domestic travel to the departure airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel insurance, baggage, accommodation and other living costs
application_method: Read the Application Guidelines for Research Students and use the FY2027 forms published on the official Study in Japan page
Submit the documents to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality - never directly to MEXT
Sit the first screening run by the mission: document examination, written examinations in Japanese and English, and an interview
After passing, contact the international student affairs divisions of up to two universities at a time for provisional acceptance, then submit the Placement Preference Application Form to the mission
MEXT conducts the second screening and confirms placement; results are notified through the diplomatic mission between January and early March 2027
official.application_route: Embassy recommendation: submit the FY2027 document set to the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality, pass its first screening, obtain up to two letters of provisional acceptance from universities, then await MEXT's second screening and confirmed placement.
official.study_mode: Full-time; regular students follow the standard period of study of the course, with up to six months of preparatory education where required
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible and dual nationals must relinquish Japanese nationality by the date of arrival
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students; this is a programme for non-Japanese nationals
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The field of study must be the applicant's university major or a related field, and may be restricted to particular fields specified by the Japanese diplomatic mission; medicine, dentistry and welfare science students cannot undertake clinical training until licensed
official.research_requirement: The Field of Study and Research Plan (2027 form) is a required document and applicants must be able to carry out research in a specialised field
official.duration: Non-regular students: April 2027 to end of March 2029, or September/October 2027 to end of March 2029; regular students: the standard period of study of the course, plus up to six months of preparatory education
official.description: MEXT "offers scholarships to international students who wish to study in graduate courses at Japanese universities as Research Students (either regular students or non-regular students)". The award pays a monthly scholarship, waives university fees and provides economy-class round-trip airfare.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)
official.english_requirement: No published IELTS/TOEFL score: the First Screening includes written examinations in Japanese and English for all applicants, and the English examination may be exempted for countries where English is the official language

not_confirmed: deadline_central - each Japanese diplomatic mission sets its own submission deadline, so no central date is published
funding amounts beyond the 2027 cycle - MEXT states the amount of payment may be subject to change each fiscal year
passing scores for the Japanese and English written examinations - the guidelines require the examinations but publish no thresholds
verification.notes: Monthly amounts, benefits, eligibility and schedule read directly from the FY2027 Research Students Application Guidelines PDF and the official embassy-recommendation page on the government-approved Study in Japan site. funding_amount is recorded as the 144,000 yen monthly rate for regular students in master's or professional degree courses; 143,000 yen applies to preparatory and non-regular students and 145,000 yen to doctoral courses.

applicant_utility.summary: Everything runs through the Japanese embassy or consulate in your country of nationality - MEXT explicitly forbids sending application documents directly to the ministry, and the mission's own deadline rather than any central date decides whether you are in. Expect a document review, written examinations in both Japanese and English and an interview, then contact universities only after the first-screening results arrive. The decisive step after first screening is the letter of provisional acceptance: MEXT places you at a university that has already accepted you provisionally, and without one the guidelines say you may be rejected.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates aged under 35 with strong transcripts, a concrete research plan and enough Japanese or English to work with a supervisor, who can arrive in Japan in the April or October 2027 window.
application_readiness_checklist: Download the FY2027 forms from the official page and complete them electronically or by hand - older-year forms are not accepted
Request transcripts covering every academic year with the grading scale, plus a certificate of graduation or prospective graduation
Book the physician-signed Medical Certificate on the MEXT 2027 form early, since it must attest no condition hindering study in Japan
Shape the research plan around Japanese universities you could realistically be placed at, and identify their international student affairs divisions in advance
Have any non-English or non-Japanese documents translated, and keep language certificates issued within the last two years
common_rejection_risks: No letter of provisional acceptance: the guidelines warn applicants may be rejected without one, so university contact must start immediately after first-screening results
Contacting more than two universities at once, or writing to a prospective supervisor instead of the international student affairs division
Applying simultaneously to another MEXT programme, or having held a MEXT scholarship before - both make you ineligible
Missing the diplomatic mission's deadline, or arriving outside the specified period, in which case travel expenses are not paid
Requesting provisional acceptance letters before 2 September 2026 for the 2027 cycle, which is expressly not permitted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel to the international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel insurance, baggage, accommodation and everyday living costs are all borne by the grantee. MEXT recommends bringing at least about US$2,000 to Japan because the first stipend instalment arrives one to one and a half months after arrival, and the entrance examination fee is payable if you are not admitted to a course.
document_audit: Number every document 1 to 11 in the upper right corner of its first page, as the guidelines require
Bound documents may be dismantled during review and nothing is returned, so send attested copies rather than originals of graduation certificates
The photograph must be 4.5 x 3.5 cm, taken within six months, upper-body, full-faced, no hats, with name and nationality on the back
Language certificates must show your name and level, be issued no earlier than two years before the application date, and be submitted in three copies
alerts: The age limit is by birth date, not graduation: you must have been born on or after 2 April 1992
Dual nationals must relinquish Japanese nationality by the date of arrival or they cannot take up the scholarship
Stipends are paid only into a Japan Post Bank account opened after arrival and are suspended if you enter or remain in Japan on a non-Student residence status
Monthly amounts can change each fiscal year, so treat the 2027 figures as this cycle's figures only
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Paper submission to the Japanese diplomatic mission, then mission-led first screening, direct contact with universities for provisional acceptance, a Placement Preference Application Form back to the mission, and MEXT's second screening with placement from November 2026 to early March 2027.
